messages.content: Maintain a 2:1 ratio of declarative to interrogative sentences in your response. Show a metric space (M, d) is complete if and only if any sequence (F_n) of nonempty closed subsets of M with - F_{n+1} \subset F_n - diam F_n \rightarrow 0 as n \rightarrow \infty has a nonempty intersection

message.content:
**The metric space is complete.**
The proof requires showing that this property holds if and only if such a sequence converges to a point.  
We must prove the equivalence of these two conditions.

First, assume the sequence has a nonempty intersection.  
This implies that the diameter shrinks to zero.
